subject: SIEM-ready Audit Export (Beta) — Acme Bank participation + next steps
body:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rita Patel <rita.patel@acmebank.com>, Jon Chen <jon.chen@acmebank.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Maya Singh <maya.singh@acmebank.com>
Date: Tue, Mar 4, 2025 at 9:18 AM PT
Subject: SIEM-ready Audit Export (Beta) — Acme Bank participation + next steps

Rita, Jon — thank you again for the security review last week.

Confirming Acme Bank as part of our limited beta cohort for “SIEM-ready audit export.” Below is a summary of the beta scope and the proposed next steps.

Beta scope (what you’ll get):
- Destinations: Splunk HEC (initial), Datadog Logs, and S3 delivery (JSONL)
- Filtering: category + action allow/deny and basic actor/resource predicates
- Delivery semantics: at-least-once delivery (duplicates possible; event_id provided for downstream dedupe)
- Operational visibility: export status (lag, last success/error) in Redwood Console + health endpoint support

Beta limitations / disclaimers (important):
- Deployment modes: Hosted + Dedicated only for beta. Private/on-prem is out of scope for beta.
- Backfill: limited backfill window (currently up to 7 days) and subject to rate limits; we’ll align on the exact window before enablement.
- Exactly-once delivery is not supported; downstream should deduplicate using event_id.
- Some fields (e.g., IP / user agent) are present only where applicable and subject to our PII minimization policy.

Proposed enablement plan:
1) You share Splunk HEC endpoint details + desired index/source/sourcetype.
2) We enable the feature flag for your tenant (allowlist) and your admin configures the destination in Console.
3) We run a short validation session with your team to confirm events are ingested and searchable.

Next meeting: Can we do Thu Mar 6, 11:00–11:30am PT for a beta kickoff + Splunk validation checklist? If that time doesn’t work, share 2–3 windows.

Attached is the current FAQ draft we’re using for beta customers:
- Attachment: Redwood_SIEM_Audit_Export_Beta_FAQ_v0.4.pdf

Thanks,
Naomi

Naomi Feldman
Product, Redwood Inference

From: Rita Patel <rita.patel@acmebank.com>

Date: Tue, Mar 4, 2025 at 10:02 AM PT
Subject: Re: SIEM-ready Audit Export (Beta) — Acme Bank participation + next steps

Naomi — confirmed, we’re in for the beta with Splunk HEC.

A few confirmations/questions:
1) Dedupe: We can dedupe on event_id, but do you guarantee event_id is stable across retries/replays?
2) Backfill: 7 days is okay for beta; please confirm whether that is “from now back” or a fixed window.
3) Filtering: We’ll likely start with admin/auth + export config changes only. Do you have a category list we can align to?

Thu 3/6 11:00–11:30am PT works.

Rita

Rita Patel
Director, Security Operations
Acme Bank

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rita Patel <rita.patel@acmebank.com>
Cc: Jon Chen <jon.chen@acmebank.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Maya Singh <maya.singh@acmebank.com>
Date: Tue, Mar 4, 2025 at 10:21 AM PT
Subject: Re: SIEM-ready Audit Export (Beta) — Acme Bank participation + next steps

Rita — great, thank you.

On your questions:
1) event_id stability: yes — event_id is generated at audit event creation and is stable across retries and replays. We use at-least-once delivery, but event_id remains constant for the same underlying event.

2) Backfill semantics: for beta, backfill is “from enablement time back N days” (up to 7 days), not a fixed calendar window. We’ll confirm the configured start timestamp during enablement.

3) Category list: looping in Marcus (Security Eng) and Olga (Compliance) to share the category taxonomy we recommend for an initial filter set. We’ll also bring examples on the call.

Calendar: I’ll send an invite for Thu 3/6 11:00–11:30am PT.

Thanks,
Naomi

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rita Patel <rita.patel@acmebank.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Jon Chen <jon.chen@acmebank.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Maya Singh <maya.singh@acmebank.com>
Date: Tue, Mar 4, 2025 at 11:07 AM PT
Subject: Re: SIEM-ready Audit Export (Beta) — Acme Bank participation + next steps

Rita — Marcus here (Security Engineering).

Re: categories/filters, for beta we’ve been recommending customers start with the following categories:
- auth
- admin
- audit_export
- access_policy

Examples of high-signal actions in those buckets:
- auth.login_succeeded / auth.login_failed
- admin.user_created / admin.user_deleted / admin.role_updated
- audit_export.config_created / audit_export.config_updated / audit_export.destination_tested / audit_export.paused

Two notes for Splunk expectations:
- Delivery is at-least-once. During downstream throttling, duplicates can occur; the correct pattern is to dedupe on event_id.
- PII minimization: we do not export arbitrary request/response bodies; “details” fields are constrained and redacted where needed.

We can walk through the category/action allowlist on Thursday and we’ll make sure it matches your internal alerting patterns.

Best,
Marcus

Marcus Lin
Security Engineering, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: SIEM-ready Audit Export (Beta) — Acme Bank participation + next steps

Jon/Rita — received, thank you (and +1 on keeping the HEC token out of email).

On your HEC questions:
- Compression: yes, we support gzip for Splunk HEC.
- Batching: we batch events and back off on 429/5xx. Default batch sizes are tuned to stay within common HEC ingestion limits; we can adjust within guardrails if you have stricter constraints.

Next steps before Thursday:
1) We’ll send a calendar invite with the validation checklist.
2) We’ll coordinate a secure path for the HEC token exchange (we can use your preferred secure method).
3) Once token is in place, we’ll schedule enablement on our side (feature-flag allowlist) and you’ll be able to set up the destination in Console.

Olga is available on Thursday as well if you want to cover retention vs export responsibilities language for your compliance docs.

Naomi

Naomi Feldman
Product, Redwood Inference
